instructions: Cut a circle out of the middle of each of the 4 slices of bread with a 2 1/2 inch biscuit cutter or the rim of a glass. Keep the circles.
Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until it foams.
Lay 2 of the bread frames and 2 of the circles in the pan, with space between them. Toast them for about 1 minute, until the undersides are light golden.
Crack 2 of the eggs into the holes, one in each frame, and sprinkle them with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Cook for about 1 minute, until the white is set on the bottom and the frame slides when you nudge it with a spatula.
Flip the frames and the circles with a thin spatula. Cook the other side for 1 minute for a runny yolk, or 2 minutes for a firmer one.
Transfer them to plates. Melt the last 1 tbsp butter in the pan and cook the other 2 frames, the other 2 circles and the last 2 eggs the same way.
Serve hot, with the toasted circles on the side.
method_notes: Both read versions cut a round from a slice of bread, toast the frame in butter, crack an egg into the hole and flip it once the bottom of the white has set. Cooking With Carlee (the lead) uses 1 tbsp butter for two slices over medium heat, toasts the bread for a minute before the eggs go in, and fries the cut out circles alongside for dipping. Tasting Table's version cuts a 2 to 3 inch hole from thicker bread and cooks each side a little longer, 2 to 3 minutes then 1 to 2. This one doubles the lead for four and cooks two at a time so the pan isn't crowded. No version had 20 or more ratings, so the first read version leads.
